provider: Indian Journal of Aerospace Medicine and AsMA
note: Both reports by K. V. Kumar match on participant stature and weight, the Bruce treadmill test and 45-minute equilibration at 15,000 ft, the leaking airlock and brief descent to about 6,000 ft, resumed exercise, left-elbow pain after descent, the unavailable hyperbaric chamber and the 65% and 50% packed-cell-volume measurements. The age, symptom timing and recovery wording differ. The 1988 paper identifies the site as the Institute of Aviation Medicine, Bangalore, India.

records.title: Decompression sickness after exercise at 4,572 m (15,000 ft) - a case report
records.locator: Case Report and Discussion, printed pp. 92–94
records.extraction_method: Visual verification of the publisher scan, printed pp. 92–95

observations.locator: Case Report and Discussion, printed pp. 92–94
observations.note: The authors assigned Allen grade 4 bends. Sweating began on reaching ground level. The paper reports left-elbow pain after 15 minutes of descent, pain remaining on day 2 and complete resolution by day 5. Nine others reportedly completed a similar protocol without the pressure mishap and cannot supply the denominator for this accident. Clinical symptom grade is distinct from Doppler VGE grade.

records.title: Decompression sickness and the role of exercise during decompression

observations.locator: Case Report, Figure 1 and Table I, printed pp. 1080–1081
observations.note: The paper reports sweating on reaching ground level, mild left-elbow pain about 10 minutes later, pain absent on the following day and complete normalization by day 3. The 1988 paper gives a Bangalore affiliation and separately lists a Houston address as the author’s current location. The case timing differs from the 1986 report and remains source-specific.
